subject: Oceanography
title: Icebergs
description: A fast breakdown of Icebergs for builders.

hook.text: Only 10% of an iceberg is visible above water—the rest lurks below, invisible and dangerous.

buildup.text: Icebergs calve from glaciers and ice shelves—breaking off as massive chunks that drift with currents.

discovery.text: Antarctic icebergs can be enormous—B-15 was the size of Jamaica when it calved in 2000.

twist.text: Icebergs fertilize the ocean—iron-rich dust trapped in the ice releases as they melt, boosting plankton growth.

climax.text: Increasing calving rates signal accelerating ice sheet loss—not just natural cycles but climate-driven change.

punchline.text: Icebergs are messengers—carrying ice sheet warnings to warmer seas.

quiz.question: How much of an iceberg is below water?
